source.text: Καὶ ὅτε ἤγγισαν εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα καὶ ἦλθον εἰς Βηθφαγὴ εἰς τὸ Ὄρος τῶν Ἐλαιῶν, τότε Ἰησοῦς ἀπέστειλεν δύο μαθητὰς λέγων αὐτοῖς· Πορεύεσθε εἰς τὴν κώμην τὴν κατέναντι ὑμῶν, καὶ εὐθέως εὑρήσετε ὄνον δεδεμένην καὶ πῶλον μετ’ αὐτῆς· λύσαντες ἀγάγετέ μοι.

records.literal_gloss: And when they drew near to Jerusalem and came to Bethphage to the Mount of the Olives, then Jesus sent two disciples, \v 2 saying to them, Go into the village the opposite you, and immediately you will find a donkey having been tied and a colt with her; having untied bring to me.

en.L: And when they drew near to Jerusalem and came to Bethphage, to the Mount of Olives, then Jesus sent two disciples, \v 2 saying to them, "Go into the village opposite you, and at once you will find a donkey tied [there], and a colt with her; untie [them and] bring [them] to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.B: When they were getting close to Jerusalem and had come to Bethphage on the Mount of Olives, Jesus sent two disciples on ahead \v 2 with instructions: "Go into the village across from you, and straightaway you will come upon a donkey tied up there with her colt. Untie them and lead them to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.R: Jesus and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers were coming near Jerusalem. They came to the village of Bethphage at the Mount of Olives. Then Jesus sent two of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers ahead. \v 2 He told them, "Go into the village in front of you. Right away you will find a donkey tied up there, with her young colt beside her. Untie them and bring them to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

es.L: Y cuando se acercaron a Jerusalén y llegaron a Betfagé, al monte de los Olivos, entonces Jesús envió a dos discípulos, \v 2 diciéndoles: «{{plural_you:Vayan|Id}} a la aldea que está frente a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, y enseguida {{plural_you:encontrarán|encontraréis}} un asna atada [allí], y un pollino con ella; una vez desatados, {{plural_you:tráiganlos|traedlos}} a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}.
es.B: Cuando ya estaban cerca de Jerusalén y habían llegado a Betfagé, en el monte de los Olivos, Jesús envió por delante a dos discípulos \v 2 con estas instrucciones: «{{plural_you:Vayan|Id}} a la aldea que {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} enfrente, y en seguida {{plural_you:encontrarán|encontraréis}} allí un asna atada junto con su cría. {{plural_you:Desátenlos|Desatadlos}} y {{plural_you:tráiganmelos|traédmelos}}.
es.R: Jesús y {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} seguidores se estaban acercando a Jerusalén. Llegaron al pueblo de Betfagé, junto al monte de los Olivos. Entonces Jesús envió por delante a dos de {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} seguidores. \v 2 Les dijo: «{{plural_you:Vayan|Id}} al pueblo que está ahí delante. Enseguida {{plural_you:encontrarán|encontraréis}} una burra atada y, a su lado, su burrito. {{plural_you:Desátenlos|Desatadlos}} y {{plural_you:tráiganmelos|traédmelos}}.

fr.L: Et quand ils approchèrent de Jérusalem et arrivèrent à Bethphagé, vers le mont des Oliviers, alors Jésus envoya deux disciples, \v 2 leur disant : « Allez au village qui est en face de vous, et aussitôt vous trouverez une ânesse attachée, et un ânon avec elle ; détachez[-les et] amenez[-les]-{{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}.
fr.B: Comme ils approchaient de Jérusalem et arrivaient à Bethphagé, sur le mont des Oliviers, Jésus envoya deux disciples en avant \v 2 avec ces instructions : « Allez au village qui est devant vous. Vous y trouverez tout de suite une ânesse attachée là, avec son ânon. Détachez-les et amenez-les-{{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}.
fr.R: Jésus et {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples approchaient de Jérusalem. Ils sont arrivés au village de Bethphagé, près du mont des Oliviers. Alors Jésus a envoyé deux de {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples en avant. \v 2 Il leur a dit : « Allez dans le village qui est devant vous. Tout de suite, vous trouverez une ânesse attachée là, avec son petit à côté d’elle. Détachez-les et amenez-les-{{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}.

sw.L: Na walipoikaribia Yerusalemu na kuwasili Bethfage, upande wa Mlima wa Mizeituni, wakati huo Yesu aliwatuma wanafunzi wawili, \v 2 akiwaambia, "Ingieni kijijini kilicho mkabala nanyi, na papo hapo mtamkuta punda jike amefungwa [huko], na mwanawe pamoja naye; mkiisha kuwafungua, waleteni {{deity_pronoun:kwangu|Kwangu}}.
sw.B: Walipokuwa wanakaribia Yerusalemu, wakiwa wamefika Bethfage kwenye Mlima wa Mizeituni, Yesu aliwatuma wanafunzi wawili watangulie, \v 2 akiwapa maagizo haya: "Nendeni kwenye kijiji kilicho mkabala nanyi, na mara moja mtamkuta punda jike amefungwa pale pamoja na mwanawe. Wafungueni, mwalete {{deity_pronoun:kwangu|Kwangu}}.
sw.R: Yesu na wafuasi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} walikuwa wanakaribia Yerusalemu. Walifika kwenye kijiji cha Bethfage, karibu na Mlima wa Mizeituni. Kisha Yesu akawatuma wafuasi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} wawili watangulie. \v 2 Akawaambia, "Nendeni katika kijiji kilicho mbele yenu. Mara moja mtamkuta punda jike amefungwa pale, na mwanawe mdogo kando yake. Wafungueni, mwalete {{deity_pronoun:kwangu|Kwangu}}.

vi.L: Và khi họ đến gần Giê-ru-sa-lem và đến Bết-pha-giê, bên núi Ô-li-ve, bấy giờ Đức Giê-xu sai hai môn đồ \v 2 và nói với họ: "Hãy đi vào làng ở trước mặt các con, và lập tức các con sẽ thấy một con lừa cái bị buộc [ở đó], và một con lừa con ở với nó; hãy mở dây [và] dắt [chúng] đến cho {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.
vi.B: Khi gần đến Giê-ru-sa-lem, họ tới làng Bết-pha-giê bên núi Ô-li-ve. Bấy giờ Đức Giê-xu sai hai môn đồ đi trước \v 2 và dặn họ: "Hãy vào làng phía trước các con. Vừa vào làng, các con sẽ thấy một con lừa cái đang bị buộc ở đó, có lừa con ở bên cạnh. Hãy mở dây và dắt chúng đến cho {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu và các môn đồ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sắp đến Giê-ru-sa-lem. Họ đến làng Bết-pha-giê, gần núi Ô-li-ve. Bấy giờ Đức Giê-xu sai hai môn đồ đi trước. \v 2 Ngài dặn họ: "Hãy vào cái làng ở phía trước các con. Ngay khi đến đó, các con sẽ thấy một con lừa cái đang bị buộc, có con lừa con của nó ở bên cạnh. Hãy mở dây và dắt chúng về cho {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.

ko.L: 그리고 그들이 예루살렘에 가까이 와서 올리브 산에 있는 벳바게에 이르렀을 때에, 그때 예수께서 제자 둘을 보내시며 \v 2 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "너희 맞은편에 있는 마을로 가거라. 그러면 곧 나귀 한 마리가 매여 있고 새끼가 그 곁에 있는 것을 보게 될 것이다. [그것들을] 풀어서 내게로 끌고 오너라.
ko.B: 그들이 예루살렘에 가까이 이르러 올리브 산 벳바게에 왔을 때, 예수께서 제자 두 사람을 먼저 보내시며 \v 2 이렇게 이르셨다. "맞은편 마을로 가거라. 거기 들어가면 곧바로 나귀 한 마리가 새끼와 함께 매여 있는 것을 보게 될 것이다. 그것들을 풀어서 내게로 끌고 오너라.
ko.R: 예수와 제자들이 예루살렘 가까이 왔다. 그들은 올리브 산에 있는 벳바게라는 마을에 이르렀다. 그때 예수께서 제자 두 사람을 먼저 보내셨다. \v 2 예수께서 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "앞에 보이는 마을로 가거라. 거기 가면 바로 나귀 한 마리가 매여 있을 것이다. 그 곁에는 어린 새끼 나귀도 있을 것이다. 그 나귀들을 풀어서 나에게 끌고 오너라.

decisions.choice: Bethphage, at the Mount of Olives: a village on the hill east of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The Mount of Olives faces Jerusalem across the Kidron Valley. Bethphage lay on its slope, on the road from Jericho, so Jesus enters the city from the east.

decisions.choice: the Mount of Olives: the place where Zechariah sees the LORD come to his city
decisions.reason: Zechariah 14:4 pictures the LORD standing on the Mount of Olives on the day he comes. The same prophet is quoted in 21:5.

decisions.choice: colt: a young donkey, the foal of the donkey that is tied
decisions.reason: The word means the young of an animal. Here it is the donkey's foal, as 21:5 makes clear.

decisions.choice: Jesus and his followers
decisions.reason: Readable names who was traveling, because the scene opens a new section.

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun spans only on separate pronouns and possessives: a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} (L); none on tráiganmelos (B, R)
alternatives: a span on every pronoun the English marks
decisions.reason: Spanish usually leaves the subject pronoun out and joins some object pronouns to the verb ("tráiganmelos"), where there is nothing separate to capitalise. So the setting covers fewer words than in English; Literal says "a mí" so the pronoun can carry it. This holds for the whole passage.

decisions.choice: plural_you spans on the words addressed to the two disciples ({{plural_you:Vayan|Id}}, {{plural_you:encontrarán|encontraréis}} and onward)
decisions.reason: Spanish has two plural forms of "you", Latin American "ustedes" and Peninsular "vosotros"; the setting chooses between them. English has no such choice, so these spans have no English counterpart. The same throughout the passage.

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B) and the passé composé (R); Matthew's historic presents kept as presents at Literal ("il leur dit")
decisions.reason: As in John, Mark 11 and Matthew 20: the passé simple is the tense of written narrative for a careful public reading, and Readable tells the story in the passé composé, as French is spoken. Speech keeps its own tenses. Literal keeps the present where Matthew tells a past event in the present, as English Literal does. This holds for the whole passage.

decisions.choice: une ânesse ... un ânon (L, B); une ânesse ... son petit (R)
alternatives: un poulain at Literal, as in Mark 11 and Luke 19
decisions.reason: Matthew names the mother donkey (the Greek word is feminine here) and the colt with her (m3), so the young animal is plainly a donkey's foal, and French has the plain word "ânon" for it. In Mark and Luke, where only the colt is named, Literal keeps the general "poulain". "Disciples" stays at every level, as in Matthew 20.

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun spans on free pronouns and possessives only ({{deity_pronoun:kwangu|Kwangu}}, {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}})
decisions.reason: The English "he" and "him" take the setting. Swahili carries them in the verb's prefixes, which cannot take a capital, so the setting applies only to free pronouns and possessives, as in John. Swahili therefore has fewer spans than English throughout the passage.

decisions.choice: punda jike; mwanawe (L, B), mwanawe mdogo (R)
decisions.reason: The tied animal is a she-donkey with her foal (meaning decision m3); "punda jike" and "mwanawe" (her young) make the pair plain at once.

decisions.choice: "Bết-pha-giê", "núi Ô-li-ve", as in Mark 11:1
decisions.reason: The forms of the Vietnamese Protestant tradition, used in the Vietnamese Mark.

decisions.choice: "con lừa cái" and "con lừa con"
decisions.reason: Matthew names two animals, the mother and her foal (21:5, 21:7); "cái" makes the mother plain.

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans in Korean, through Matthew 21:1-17; the narrative honours Jesus with "께서" and -시-, Jesus speaks in 해라체
decisions.reason: Korean has no capital letters, so the deity_pronoun setting has nothing to change (style guide, sections 4 and 7).

decisions.choice: "올리브 산"; "벳바게"; "새끼" (L, B), "어린 새끼 나귀" (R); "곧" (L), "곧바로" (B), "바로" (R)
decisions.reason: The words of the Korean Mark 11:1-2: "올리브 산" is the modern word the style guide prefers, "벳바게" the Protestant form. The colt is the foal of the tied donkey (meaning decision). Euthys takes the settled Korean Gospel forms.

decisions.choice: [그것들을]
decisions.reason: The Greek leaves the object of "untie" and "bring" to be understood; Korean needs it, and Literal brackets it.

source.text: καὶ ἐάν τις ὑμῖν εἴπῃ τι, ἐρεῖτε ὅτι Ὁ κύριος αὐτῶν χρείαν ἔχει· εὐθὺς δὲ ἀποστελεῖ αὐτούς.

records.literal_gloss: And if anyone to you says anything, you will say that The Lord of them need has; immediately then he will send them.

en.L: And if anyone says anything to you, you will say, 'The Lord has need of them,' and immediately he will send them."
en.B: If anyone questions you, say, 'The Lord needs them.' Then he will let them go at once."
en.R: If anyone asks you about it, say, 'The Lord needs them.' Then the owner will let you take them right away."

es.L: Y si alguien {{plural_you:les|os}} dice algo, {{plural_you:dirán|diréis}}: “El Señor tiene necesidad de ellos”, y al instante los enviará».
es.B: Si alguien {{plural_you:les|os}} pregunta algo, {{plural_you:díganle|decidle}}: “El Señor los necesita”. Y enseguida los dejará ir».
es.R: Si alguien {{plural_you:les|os}} pregunta por qué, {{plural_you:díganle|decidle}}: “El Señor los necesita”. Entonces el dueño {{plural_you:les|os}} dejará llevárselos enseguida».

fr.L: Et si quelqu’un vous dit quelque chose, vous direz : “Le Seigneur en a besoin”, et aussitôt il les enverra. »
fr.B: Si quelqu’un vous pose une question, répondez : “Le Seigneur en a besoin.” Et il les laissera partir aussitôt. »
fr.R: Si quelqu’un vous demande ce que vous faites, dites-lui : “Le Seigneur en a besoin.” Alors le propriétaire vous laissera les emmener tout de suite. »

sw.L: Na kama mtu akiwaambia lolote, mtasema, 'Bwana anawahitaji,' na mara moja atawatuma."
sw.B: Mtu yeyote akiwauliza, mwambieni, 'Bwana anawahitaji.' Naye atawaachia mara moja."
sw.R: Mtu yeyote akiwauliza habari yake, mwambieni, 'Bwana anawahitaji.' Ndipo mwenye punda atawaruhusu mwachukue mara moja."

vi.L: Và nếu có ai nói gì với các con, các con sẽ nói: 'Chúa cần đến chúng', và lập tức người ấy sẽ gửi chúng đi."
vi.B: Nếu có ai hỏi gì các con, hãy trả lời: 'Chúa cần chúng.' Người ta sẽ để cho các con dắt đi ngay."
vi.R: Nếu có ai hỏi các con về việc ấy, hãy nói: 'Chúa cần chúng.' Thế là người chủ sẽ để các con dắt chúng đi ngay."

ko.L: 그리고 누가 너희에게 무슨 말을 하면, 너희는 '주님께서 그것들이 필요하십니다' 하고 말할 것이다. 그러면 그가 곧 그것들을 보내 줄 것이다."
ko.B: 누가 너희에게 무엇이라고 하거든, '주님께서 쓰시려고 하십니다' 하고 말하여라. 그러면 그 사람이 곧 보내 줄 것이다."
ko.R: 누가 너희에게 왜 그러느냐고 묻거든, '주님께서 쓰실 데가 있으십니다' 하고 말하여라. 그러면 나귀 주인이 바로 나귀들을 끌고 가게 해 줄 것이다."

decisions.choice: the Lord: Jesus speaks of himself
decisions.reason: Matthew uses this title for Jesus in the mouth of those who trust him (8:2; 8:25). The owner's consent shows that he recognizes the claim.

decisions.choice: of them: goes with need (he has need of them)
decisions.reason: The pronoun can go with "the Lord" or with "need". The sense "their master needs them" would make the owner the speaker's lord, which does not fit the story.

decisions.choice: he will send them: the owner will let the animals go at once
alternatives: Jesus will send them back promptly
decisions.reason: Mark 11:3 has a similar line that may mean Jesus will return the colt. In Matthew the subject is most naturally the person who asks.

decisions.choice: the owner
decisions.reason: Readable says who will let the animals go.

decisions.choice: "il les enverra" with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: As the English reads it (m3, uncertain), the one who sends the animals is their owner, not Jesus, so the pronoun is plain.

decisions.choice: "Chúa" for "the Lord", with no setting
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks of himself as Lord, as in Mark 11:3; the word is a title, not a pronoun.

decisions.choice: "người ấy" (L); "người ta" (B); "người chủ" (R) for the one who will send them
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads the sender as the owner, who will let the animals go; unlike Mark 11:3, it is not Jesus sending them back.

decisions.choice: The disciples' message to strangers in 합쇼체, with the honorific for "the Lord" ("주님께서 ... 필요하십니다")
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks of himself as the Lord (meaning decision); the words are what the disciples will say to the villagers, so they are polite and honour the Lord they speak of, as in the Korean Mark 11:3. Literal keeps the future "you will say".

ko.L: 그런데 이 일이 일어난 것은 예언자를 통하여 하신 말씀이 이루어지게 하려는 것이었다. [그 말씀은] 이러하다.

ko.R: 이렇게 해서 예언자가 한 말이 이루어졌다.

decisions.choice: the prophet: Zechariah, whose words follow, opened with a line of Isaiah
decisions.reason: The words of 21:5 are Zechariah 9:9, introduced by a phrase from Isaiah 62:11. Matthew names no prophet here.

decisions.choice: the same wording as 1:22, 2:15 and 4:14
decisions.reason: The formula that introduces a fulfilled prophecy is given in the same words each time.

decisions.choice: "được ứng nghiệm" (L), "ứng nghiệm" (B); "trở thành sự thật" (R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for Matthew's fulfilment formula (1:22, 8:17).

decisions.choice: The fulfilment formula worded as in the Korean Matthew 4:14
decisions.reason: Matthew repeats the formula (1:22; 2:15; 4:14), and the English keeps one wording for it; Korean does the same, with "이루어지다", "이루다" as settled for the Korean Matthew.

source.text: Εἴπατε τῇ θυγατρὶ Σιών· Ἰδοὺ ὁ βασιλεύς σου ἔρχεταί σοι πραῢς καὶ ἐπιβεβηκὼς ἐπὶ ὄνον καὶ ἐπὶ πῶλον υἱὸν ὑποζυγίου.

records.literal_gloss: Say to the daughter of Zion, Behold the king of you comes to you, gentle and having mounted on a donkey and on a colt a son of a beast of burden.

en.L: "Say to the daughter of Zion, 'Look, your king is coming to you, gentle and mounted on a donkey, and on a colt, [the] foal of a beast of burden.'"
en.B: "Tell the daughter of Zion, 'Your king is coming to you! He is gentle, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is seated on a donkey and on a colt, the foal of a pack animal.'"
en.R: "Tell the people of Jerusalem, 'Look! Your king is coming to you. He is gentle. He is riding on a donkey and on a young donkey, a colt.'"

es.L: «{{plural_you:Digan|Decid}} a la hija de Sion: “Mira, tu rey viene a ti, manso y montado sobre un asna, y sobre un pollino, cría de una bestia de carga”».
es.B: «{{plural_you:Digan|Decid}} a la hija de Sion: “¡Tu rey viene a ti! Es manso, y viene montado en un asna y en un pollino, cría de un animal de carga”».
es.R: «{{plural_you:Digan|Decid}} a la gente de Jerusalén: “¡{{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}}! {{plural_you:Su|Vuestro}} rey viene a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. Es manso. Viene montado en una burra y en un burrito, su cría”».

fr.L: « Dites à la fille de Sion : “Voici, ton roi vient à toi, doux et monté sur une ânesse, et sur un ânon, le petit d’une bête de somme.” »
fr.B: « Dites à la fille de Sion : “Ton roi vient à toi ! Il est doux, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est monté sur une ânesse et sur un ânon, le petit d’une bête de somme.” »
fr.R: « Dites aux habitants de Jérusalem : “Regardez ! Votre roi vient vers vous. Il est doux. Il est monté sur une ânesse et sur un ânon, un jeune âne.” »

sw.L: "Mwambieni binti Sayuni, 'Tazama, mfalme wako anakujia, ni mpole, na amepanda juu ya punda, na juu ya mwana-punda, mtoto wa mnyama wa mizigo.'"
sw.B: "Mwambieni binti Sayuni, 'Mfalme wako anakujia! Yeye ni mpole, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} ameketi juu ya punda, na juu ya mwana-punda, mtoto wa mnyama wa mizigo.'"
sw.R: "Waambieni watu wa Yerusalemu, 'Tazameni! Mfalme wenu anakuja kwenu. Yeye ni mpole. Amepanda punda, na mwana-punda mdogo.'"

vi.L: "Hãy nói với con gái Si-ôn: 'Kìa, Vua của ngươi đến với ngươi, hiền lành và cưỡi trên lừa, trên một con lừa con, con của lừa chở hàng.'"
vi.B: "Hãy nói với con gái Si-ôn: 'Vua của ngươi đang đến với ngươi! Ngài hiền lành, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cưỡi trên lưng lừa, trên một con lừa con, là con của lừa chở hàng.'"
vi.R: "Hãy nói với dân thành Giê-ru-sa-lem: 'Kìa! Vua của các ngươi đang đến với các ngươi. Ngài hiền lành. Ngài cưỡi trên một con lừa, trên một con lừa con.'"

ko.L: "시온의 딸에게 말하여라. '보라, 네 왕이 네게 오신다. 그분은 온유하시며, 나귀와 짐 나르는 짐승의 새끼인 어린 나귀를 타고 계신다.'"
ko.B: "시온의 딸에게 말하여라. '네 왕이 네게 오신다! 그분은 온유하시며, 나귀와 짐 나르는 짐승의 새끼인 어린 나귀를 타셨다.'"
ko.R: "예루살렘 사람들에게 말하여라. '보아라! 너희 왕이 너희에게 오신다. 그분은 겸손하시다. 그분은 나귀를 타고 오신다. 어린 새끼 나귀를 타고 오신다.'"

decisions.choice: Isaiah 62:11 and Zechariah 9:9
decisions.reason: "Say to the daughter of Zion" opens Isaiah 62:11; the rest is Zechariah 9:9. Matthew leaves out Zechariah's words about the king being righteous and bringing salvation, and keeps the word gentle.

decisions.choice: the daughter of Zion: Jerusalem and its people
alternatives: a young woman of the city
decisions.reason: The prophets speak of a city as a daughter. Zion is the hill of the temple and stands for the whole city.

decisions.choice: gentle: meek, not proud or violent
decisions.reason: It is the word of 5:5 and 11:29. A king who comes on a donkey, not a war horse, comes in peace (Zechariah 9:10).

decisions.choice: on a donkey and on a colt: Matthew names two animals
decisions.reason: In Hebrew poetry the second line names the same donkey again. Matthew's story has two animals (21:2, 7) and reads the words that way.

decisions.choice: look (L, R); not rendered (B)
decisions.reason: Literal and Readable keep the call to look; Balanced carries its force with an exclamation.

decisions.choice: spans on he for the king
decisions.reason: The king is Jesus, so pronouns for him take the deity_pronoun setting, as with the servant in 12:18-21.

decisions.choice: the people of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Readable says who is meant.

decisions.choice: {{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}}, {{plural_you:Su|Vuestro}}, {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable says who "the daughter of Zion" is (meaning decision m2). Addressed to many, its "you" takes the ustedes / vosotros setting, as at John 12:15.

decisions.choice: "Votre roi vient vers vous" at Readable
decisions.reason: Readable names the people of Jerusalem (m2), a plural, so French says "vous" to them where Literal and Balanced keep "toi" for the daughter of Zion.

decisions.choice: "con gái Si-ôn" (L, B); "dân thành Giê-ru-sa-lem" (R)
decisions.reason: The daughter of Zion is Jerusalem and its people; Readable says so, as the English Readable does. The city is addressed as "ngươi" (L, B), "các ngươi" (R).

decisions.choice: "{{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}" for the king, and "Vua" with a capital
decisions.reason: The king of the prophecy is Jesus, whose entry fulfils it, so the pronoun takes the setting, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "보라" (L), not rendered (B), "보아라" (R); the king takes the honorific ("오신다", "그분")
decisions.reason: Where the English has deity_pronoun spans for the king, Korean honours him with -시- and "그분", since the king is Jesus; Korean has no capital letters for the setting to change.

decisions.choice: "시온의 딸" (L, B), "예루살렘 사람들" (R); "온유하다" (L, B), "겸손하다" (R)
decisions.reason: The daughter of Zion is Jerusalem and its people (meaning decision); Readable says so, as the English does. Gentle is meek, not proud or violent (meaning decision).

source.text: πορευθέντες δὲ οἱ μαθηταὶ καὶ ποιήσαντες καθὼς συνέταξεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἤγαγον τὴν ὄνον καὶ τὸν πῶλον, καὶ ἐπέθηκαν ἐπ’ αὐτῶν τὰ ἱμάτια, καὶ ἐπεκάθισεν ἐπάνω αὐτῶν.

records.literal_gloss: Having gone then the disciples and having done as directed them the Jesus \v 7 they brought the donkey and the colt, and they put on them the cloaks, and he sat on them.

en.L: And the disciples went and did just as Jesus had directed them; \v 7 they brought the donkey and the colt and put their cloaks on them, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sat on them.
en.B: The disciples went off and did what Jesus had told them. \v 7 They brought the donkey and the colt and laid their cloaks on them, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sat on them.
en.R: The two followers went and did what Jesus had told them to do. \v 7 They brought the donkey and the colt to Jesus. They put their coats on the animals, and Jesus sat on them.

es.L: Y habiendo ido los discípulos y habiendo hecho tal como Jesús les había mandado, \v 7 trajeron el asna y el pollino, y pusieron encima de ellos los mantos, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} se sentó sobre ellos.
es.B: Los discípulos fueron e hicieron lo que Jesús les había indicado. \v 7 Trajeron el asna y el pollino, les echaron encima sus mantos, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} se sentó sobre ellos.
es.R: Los dos seguidores fueron e hicieron lo que Jesús les había dicho. \v 7 Llevaron a Jesús la burra y el burrito. Pusieron sus mantos sobre los animales, y Jesús se sentó encima.

fr.L: Et les disciples, étant partis et ayant fait comme Jésus le leur avait ordonné, \v 7 amenèrent l’ânesse et l’ânon, et mirent sur eux leurs manteaux, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} s’assit dessus.
fr.B: Les disciples s’en allèrent et firent ce que Jésus leur avait dit. \v 7 Ils amenèrent l’ânesse et l’ânon, posèrent sur eux leurs manteaux, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} s’assit dessus.
fr.R: Les deux disciples sont partis et ils ont fait ce que Jésus leur avait dit de faire. \v 7 Ils ont amené l’ânesse et l’ânon à Jésus. Ils ont mis leurs manteaux sur le dos des animaux, et Jésus s’est assis dessus.

sw.L: Basi wanafunzi wakaenda, na baada ya kufanya sawasawa na alivyowaagiza Yesu, \v 7 waliwaleta punda jike na mwana-punda, wakatandika mavazi juu yao, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} akaketi juu yao.
sw.B: Wanafunzi walikwenda, wakafanya kama Yesu alivyowaagiza. \v 7 Wakawaleta punda jike na mwana-punda, wakatandika mavazi yao juu ya wanyama hao, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} akaketi juu yao.
sw.R: Wale wafuasi wawili walikwenda, wakafanya kama Yesu alivyowaambia. \v 7 Wakamletea Yesu punda jike na mwana-punda. Wakatandika makoti yao juu ya wanyama hao, na Yesu akaketi juu yao.

vi.L: Các môn đồ đi và làm đúng như Đức Giê-xu đã truyền cho họ; \v 7 họ dắt lừa cái và lừa con về, đặt áo ngoài của mình lên chúng, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ngồi lên trên.
vi.B: Các môn đồ đi và làm đúng như Đức Giê-xu đã dặn. \v 7 Họ dắt lừa cái và lừa con về, trải áo ngoài của mình lên lưng chúng, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ngồi lên.
vi.R: Hai môn đồ đi và làm đúng như Đức Giê-xu đã dặn. \v 7 Họ dắt lừa cái và lừa con đến với Đức Giê-xu. Họ trải áo khoác của mình lên lưng hai con lừa, và Đức Giê-xu ngồi lên.

ko.L: 그리고 제자들이 가서 예수께서 그들에게 지시하신 대로 하여, \v 7 나귀와 새끼를 끌고 왔다. 그리고 그 위에 자기들의 겉옷을 얹었고, 그분은 그 위에 앉으셨다.
ko.B: 제자들은 가서 예수께서 일러 주신 대로 했다. \v 7 그들은 나귀와 새끼를 끌고 와서 그 위에 자기들의 겉옷을 얹었다. 예수께서 그 위에 앉으셨다.
ko.R: 두 제자는 가서 예수께서 하라고 하신 대로 했다. \v 7 그들은 나귀와 새끼 나귀를 예수께 끌고 왔다. 그리고 자기들의 겉옷을 나귀 등에 얹었다. 예수께서 그 위에 타셨다.

decisions.choice: he sat on them: most likely on the cloaks laid over the animals
decisions.reason: The nearest plural is the cloaks. Matthew does not say how Jesus rode; the words need not mean he sat on two animals.

decisions.choice: cloaks: the outer garments, laid on as a saddle
decisions.reason: The disciples use their own outer clothing to make a seat, an act of honor.

decisions.choice: on the animals; Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear what the cloaks were put on and who sat.

decisions.choice: "áo ngoài" (L, B); "áo khoác" (R) for the cloaks
decisions.reason: As in Mark 11:7-8 and Matthew 5:40.

decisions.choice: "겉옷"; "그 위에 앉으셨다" (L, B), "그 위에 타셨다" (R)
decisions.reason: The cloaks were outer garments laid on as a saddle (meaning decision), "겉옷" as in the Korean Mark 11:7. "그 위에" leaves open whether "them" is the cloaks or the animals, as the Greek does; the meaning decision takes it as the cloaks.

source.text: ὁ δὲ πλεῖστος ὄχλος ἔστρωσαν ἑαυτῶν τὰ ἱμάτια ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ, ἄλλοι δὲ ἔκοπτον κλάδους ἀπὸ τῶν δένδρων καὶ ἐστρώννυον ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ.

records.literal_gloss: The then very large crowd spread their own the cloaks on the road, others then were cutting branches from the trees and were spreading on the road.

en.L: And the very large crowd spread their own cloaks on the road, and others were cutting branches from the trees and spreading [them] on the road.
en.B: The crowd, which was very large, spread their own cloaks across the road, and others kept cutting branches from the trees and laying them on the road.
en.R: The huge crowd spread their coats on the road. Other people cut branches from the trees and spread them on the road too.

es.L: Y la enorme multitud extendió sus propios mantos en el camino; otros cortaban ramas de los árboles y [las] esparcían por el camino.
es.B: La multitud, que era muy grande, extendió sus mantos sobre el camino, y otros iban cortando ramas de los árboles y alfombrando con ellas el camino.
es.R: La enorme multitud puso sus mantos en el camino. Otras personas cortaron ramas de los árboles y también las pusieron en el camino.

fr.L: Et la foule, très nombreuse, étendit ses propres manteaux sur le chemin, et d’autres coupaient des branches aux arbres et [les] étendaient sur le chemin.
fr.B: La foule, qui était très nombreuse, étendit ses manteaux sur la route, et d’autres coupaient des branches aux arbres et les étendaient sur la route.
fr.R: Il y avait une foule immense. Les gens ont étendu leurs manteaux sur la route. D’autres ont coupé des branches aux arbres et les ont étendues aussi sur la route.

sw.L: Na umati mkubwa sana ulitandika mavazi yao wenyewe njiani, na wengine walikuwa wakikata matawi ya miti na kuyatandaza njiani.
sw.B: Umati, uliokuwa mkubwa sana, ulitandaza mavazi yao barabarani, na wengine waliendelea kukata matawi ya miti na kuyatandaza barabarani.
sw.R: Umati mkubwa wa watu ulitandika makoti yao barabarani. Watu wengine walikata matawi ya miti, wakayatandika barabarani pia.

vi.L: Phần đông dân chúng trải áo ngoài của mình trên đường, còn những người khác chặt cành cây và rải trên đường.
vi.B: Đoàn dân rất đông trải áo ngoài của mình trên đường, những người khác thì chặt cành cây và rải ra trên đường.
vi.R: Rất đông người trải áo khoác của mình trên đường. Những người khác chặt cành cây và rải trên đường nữa.

ko.L: 그리고 아주 많은 무리가 자기들의 겉옷을 길에 폈고, 다른 사람들은 나무에서 가지들을 꺾어 길에 펴고 있었다.
ko.B: 무리는 아주 많았는데, 그들은 자기들의 겉옷을 길에 깔았다. 또 다른 사람들은 나무에서 가지를 계속 꺾어다가 길에 깔았다.
ko.R: 아주 많은 사람이 자기 겉옷을 길에 깔았다. 또 어떤 사람들은 나뭇가지를 꺾어서 길에 깔았다.

decisions.choice: the very large crowd
decisions.reason: The word is a superlative. With a group it can mean the greater part of it; here it more likely describes the size of the crowd.

decisions.choice: cloaks spread on the road: a welcome for a king
alternatives: a way to keep the dust down
decisions.reason: When Jehu was made king, the people spread their cloaks under him (2 Kings 9:13). Branches were waved at festivals and victories (1 Maccabees 13:51).

decisions.choice: coats
decisions.reason: Readable uses a common word for an outer garment.

source.text: οἱ δὲ ὄχλοι οἱ προάγοντες αὐτὸν καὶ οἱ ἀκολουθοῦντες ἔκραζον λέγοντες· Ὡσαννὰ τῷ υἱῷ Δαυίδ· Εὐλογημένος ὁ ἐρχόμενος ἐν ὀνόματι κυρίου· Ὡσαννὰ ἐν τοῖς ὑψίστοις.

records.literal_gloss: The then crowds the going before him and the following were crying out saying, Hosanna to the son of David; blessed the coming in name of Lord; Hosanna in the highest.

en.L: And the crowds going ahead of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and those following were crying out, saying, "Hosanna to the Son of David! Blessed [is] the one coming in [the] name of [the] Lord! Hosanna in the highest!"
en.B: Crowds walked in front of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and behind {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and they kept shouting, "Hosanna to the Son of David! Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord! Hosanna in the highest heavens!"
en.R: Crowds of people walked ahead of Jesus and behind {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. They were shouting, "Hosanna to the Son of David! May God bless the one who comes in the name of the Lord! Hosanna to God in heaven!"

es.L: Y las multitudes que iban delante de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} y las que seguían gritaban, diciendo: «¡Hosanna al Hijo de David! ¡Bendito el que viene en [el] nombre del Señor! ¡Hosanna en las alturas!».
es.B: Las multitudes iban delante y detrás de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, y gritaban sin cesar: «¡Hosanna al Hijo de David! ¡Bendito el que viene en el nombre del Señor! ¡Hosanna en lo más alto de los cielos!».
es.R: Mucha gente caminaba delante de Jesús y detrás de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}. Gritaban: «¡Hosanna al Hijo de David! ¡Que Dios bendiga al que viene en el nombre del Señor! ¡Hosanna a Dios en el cielo!».

fr.L: Et les foules qui allaient devant {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} et celles qui suivaient criaient, disant : « Hosanna au Fils de David ! Béni [soit] celui qui vient au nom du Seigneur ! Hosanna dans les lieux très hauts ! »
fr.B: Les foules qui marchaient devant {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} et celles qui venaient derrière ne cessaient de crier : « Hosanna au Fils de David ! Béni soit celui qui vient au nom du Seigneur ! Hosanna au plus haut des cieux ! »
fr.R: Des foules de gens marchaient devant Jésus, et d’autres derrière {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. Ils criaient : « Hosanna au Fils de David ! Que Dieu bénisse celui qui vient au nom du Seigneur ! Hosanna à Dieu dans le ciel ! »

sw.L: Na makundi ya watu yaliyokuwa yakimtangulia na yale yaliyokuwa yakifuata yalikuwa yakipaza sauti, yakisema, "Hosana kwa Mwana wa Daudi! [Amebarikiwa] anayekuja kwa jina la Bwana! Hosana katika [mbingu] zilizo juu kabisa!"
sw.B: Makundi ya watu yalitembea mbele {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} na nyuma {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, yakipaza sauti bila kukoma, "Hosana kwa Mwana wa Daudi! Amebarikiwa yeye anayekuja kwa jina la Bwana! Hosana juu kabisa mbinguni!"
sw.R: Makundi ya watu yalitembea mbele ya Yesu na nyuma {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}. Walikuwa wakipaza sauti, "Hosana kwa Mwana wa Daudi! Mungu ambariki yeye anayekuja kwa jina la Bwana! Hosana kwa Mungu aliye mbinguni!"

vi.L: Và đoàn dân đi trước {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và những người theo sau đều kêu lên rằng: "Hô-sa-na Con của Đa-vít! Đáng chúc tụng [thay] Đấng đến trong danh [của] Chúa! Hô-sa-na trên nơi chí cao!"
vi.B: Đoàn dân đi trước và theo sau {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cứ reo hò: "Hô-sa-na Con của Đa-vít! Chúc tụng Đấng đến trong danh Chúa! Hô-sa-na trên các tầng trời cao nhất!"
vi.R: Có rất nhiều người đi trước Đức Giê-xu, và nhiều người theo sau {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Họ cứ reo hò: "Hô-sa-na Con vua Đa-vít! Cầu Đức Chúa Trời ban phước cho Đấng đến trong danh Chúa! Hô-sa-na, ngợi khen Đức Chúa Trời trên trời cao!"

ko.L: 그리고 그분 앞에서 가는 무리와 뒤따르는 [무리가] 소리 질러 말하고 있었다. "다윗의 자손께 호산나! 주님의 이름으로 오시는 분께 복이 있기를! 가장 높은 곳에서 호산나!"
ko.B: 예수 앞에서 가는 무리와 뒤따르는 무리가 계속 외쳤다. "다윗의 자손께 호산나! 주님의 이름으로 오시는 분께 복이 있기를! 가장 높은 하늘에서 호산나!"
ko.R: 예수 앞에서 걸어가는 사람들도 있었고, 뒤에서 따라오는 사람들도 있었다. 그들은 계속 외쳤다. "다윗의 자손께 호산나! 주님께서 보내셔서 오시는 분께 하나님께서 복을 주시기를! 가장 높은 하늘에 계신 하나님께 호산나!"

decisions.choice: Hosanna: a Hebrew cry meaning save, please, used as a shout of praise
alternatives: a simple cheer with no meaning
decisions.reason: The word comes from Psalm 118:25, "save us, please". Sung at the great feasts, it had become a cry of praise and welcome as well as a prayer.

decisions.choice: blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord: Psalm 118:26
decisions.reason: The psalm was sung by pilgrims going up to the temple. Where Matthew has "Lord", the Hebrew has God's name, the LORD. The crowds apply the words to Jesus as the king who comes.

decisions.choice: Son of David: the king promised from David's family
decisions.reason: God promised David a son whose kingdom would last forever (2 Samuel 7:12-16). The crowds hail Jesus as that king (see 1:1; 12:23).

decisions.choice: in the highest: in the highest heavens, where God is
decisions.reason: The cry calls on God in heaven, or on those in heaven to join the praise (Psalm 148:1-2).

decisions.choice: Hosanna at every level
decisions.reason: The word is a cry of both prayer and praise. Every level keeps it, and the meaning decision explains it.

decisions.choice: May God bless the one who comes; to God in heaven
alternatives: Blessed is the one coming; in the highest
decisions.reason: Readable says who blesses and where the praise is directed.

decisions.choice: ¡Hosanna! at every level; el Señor
decisions.reason: As in English and at John 12:13: the cry keeps its own word (meaning decision m1). In Psalm 118:26 "Lord" stands for God's own name (meaning decision m2); Spanish Bibles use "el Señor" for it.

decisions.choice: dans les lieux très hauts (L); au plus haut des cieux (B); à Dieu dans le ciel (R)
alternatives: au plus haut des cieux at Literal
decisions.reason: As in Mark 11:10 and Luke 19:38: Literal keeps the plural place-word, Balanced says plainly that it is the highest heaven (m4), and Readable says to whom the praise goes, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: Hosana at every level; Bwana
decisions.reason: As at John 12:13: "Hosana" is kept at every level, as the English keeps "Hosanna" (meaning decision m1). "Bwana" here stands for God, as in Psalm 118 (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: "Hô-sa-na" at every level; the blessing and "in the highest" as in the Vietnamese Mark 11:9-10
decisions.reason: Keeps the Hebrew cry in the Vietnamese spelling of the tradition; the other words match the parallel in Mark at each level.

decisions.choice: "Con của Đa-vít" (L, B); "Con vua Đa-vít" (R)
decisions.reason: As in Matthew 9:27 and 12:23.

decisions.choice: "호산나" at every level; "다윗의 자손께"; "...께 복이 있기를!"
decisions.reason: As in the Korean Mark 11:9-10 and John 12:13: the Hebrew cry is kept (meaning decision), the Son of David is honoured with "께", and the blessing is a modern wish a crowd could shout. Readable says to whom the praise goes, as the English does.

decisions.choice: [무리가]
decisions.reason: The Greek has one article for "those following"; Korean needs the noun again, and Literal brackets it.

source.text: καὶ εἰσελθόντος αὐτοῦ εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα ἐσείσθη πᾶσα ἡ πόλις λέγουσα· Τίς ἐστιν οὗτος;

records.literal_gloss: And having entered of him into Jerusalem was stirred all the city saying, Who is this?

en.L: And when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} entered Jerusalem, the whole city was shaken, saying, "Who is this?"
en.B: When {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} came into Jerusalem, the whole city was in an uproar. "Who is this man?" people asked.
en.R: When Jesus went into Jerusalem, everyone in the city was stirred up. They asked, "Who is this man?"

es.L: Y al entrar {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} en Jerusalén, se estremeció toda la ciudad, diciendo: «¿Quién es este?».
es.B: Cuando {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} entró en Jerusalén, toda la ciudad se alborotó. «¿Quién es este hombre?», preguntaba la gente.
es.R: Cuando Jesús entró en Jerusalén, toda la gente de la ciudad se agitó. Preguntaban: «¿Quién es este hombre?».

fr.L: Et quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} entra dans Jérusalem, toute la ville fut ébranlée, disant : « Qui est celui-ci ? »
fr.B: Quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} entra dans Jérusalem, toute la ville fut en effervescence. « Qui est cet homme ? » demandait-on.
fr.R: Quand Jésus est entré dans Jérusalem, toute la ville a été en émoi. Les gens demandaient : « Qui est cet homme ? »

sw.L: Na {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} alipoingia Yerusalemu, mji wote ulitikiswa, ukisema, "Huyu ni nani?"
sw.B: Alipoingia Yerusalemu, mji mzima ulichafuka. Watu wakauliza, "Mtu huyu ni nani?"
sw.R: Yesu alipoingia Yerusalemu, watu wote wa mji walishtuka. Wakauliza, "Mtu huyu ni nani?"

vi.L: Và khi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} vào Giê-ru-sa-lem, cả thành đều rúng động mà nói: "Người này là ai?"
vi.B: Khi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} vào Giê-ru-sa-lem, cả thành náo động. Người ta hỏi: "Người này là ai vậy?"
vi.R: Khi Đức Giê-xu vào Giê-ru-sa-lem, cả thành xôn xao. Người ta hỏi nhau: "Người này là ai vậy?"

ko.L: 그리고 그분이 예루살렘에 들어가시자, 온 성이 술렁이며 말했다. "이 사람이 누구냐?"
ko.B: 예수께서 예루살렘에 들어가시자, 온 성이 떠들썩해졌다. 사람들이 물었다. "이 사람이 누구냐?"
ko.R: 예수께서 예루살렘에 들어가시자, 도시 사람들이 모두 술렁거렸다. 그들이 물었다. "이 사람이 누구냐?"

decisions.choice: was shaken: stirred up, in turmoil
decisions.reason: The verb is used of an earthquake (27:51; 28:4). All Jerusalem was troubled in the same way when the magi asked about the king (2:3).

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus.

decisions.choice: "Người này" for "this one", with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: The people of the city do not yet know who he is; as in Matthew 8:27.

decisions.choice: "술렁이다" (L), "떠들썩해지다" (B), "술렁거리다" (R); "성" (L, B), "도시" (R)
decisions.reason: Shaken here is stirred up, in turmoil (meaning decision). "성" for the walled city as in the Korean Mark 11:19, "도시" at Readable. The question among the townspeople is in the plain style.

source.text: οἱ δὲ ὄχλοι ἔλεγον· Οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ προφήτης Ἰησοῦς ὁ ἀπὸ Ναζαρὲθ τῆς Γαλιλαίας.

records.literal_gloss: The then crowds were saying, This is the prophet Jesus the from Nazareth of Galilee.

en.L: And the crowds were saying, "This is the prophet Jesus, the one from Nazareth of Galilee."
en.B: And the crowds kept saying, "This is the prophet, Jesus, the man from Nazareth in Galilee."
en.R: The crowds said, "This is Jesus, the prophet. He comes from the town of Nazareth in Galilee."

es.L: Y las multitudes decían: «Este es el profeta Jesús, el de Nazaret de Galilea».
es.B: Y las multitudes respondían: «Este es el profeta, Jesús, el de Nazaret de Galilea».
es.R: La gente decía: «Este es Jesús, el profeta. Es del pueblo de Nazaret, en Galilea».

fr.L: Et les foules disaient : « Celui-ci est le prophète Jésus, celui de Nazareth de Galilée. »
fr.B: Et les foules répondaient : « C’est le prophète Jésus, de Nazareth en Galilée. »
fr.R: Les foules disaient : « C’est Jésus, le prophète. Il vient de la ville de Nazareth, en Galilée. »

sw.L: Na makundi ya watu yalikuwa yakisema, "Huyu ndiye nabii Yesu, aliyetoka Nazareti ya Galilaya."
sw.B: Na makundi ya watu yakaendelea kusema, "Huyu ni nabii, Yesu, mtu wa Nazareti katika Galilaya."
sw.R: Watu wakasema, "Huyu ni Yesu, yule nabii. Anatoka katika mji wa Nazareti huko Galilaya."

vi.L: Và đoàn dân nói: "Đây là nhà tiên tri Giê-xu, người từ Na-xa-rét thuộc Ga-li-lê."
vi.B: Đoàn dân đáp: "Đây là nhà tiên tri Giê-xu, người Na-xa-rét, xứ Ga-li-lê."
vi.R: Đoàn dân nói: "Đây là Giê-xu, nhà tiên tri. Ông đến từ thị trấn Na-xa-rét ở miền Ga-li-lê."

ko.L: 그러자 무리가 말하고 있었다. "이분은 갈릴리 나사렛에서 오신 예언자 예수이시다."
ko.B: 무리가 대답했다. "이분은 예언자 예수이시다. 갈릴리 나사렛에서 오신 분이다."
ko.R: 사람들이 말했다. "이분은 예언자 예수이시다. 갈릴리 지방의 나사렛 마을에서 오셨다."

decisions.choice: the prophet: a prophet sent by God, perhaps the prophet Moses promised
decisions.reason: The crowds hold Jesus to be a prophet (21:46). The article may point to the prophet like Moses (Deuteronomy 18:15), but the crowds may mean no more than a known prophet.

decisions.choice: from Nazareth of Galilee: his hometown in the north
decisions.reason: Jesus grew up in Nazareth (2:23). The pilgrims from Galilee name him by his town.

decisions.choice: "Giê-xu" without "Đức", and "ông" (R), in the crowd's words
decisions.reason: The crowds speak of him as a prophet from Nazareth, not with the reverence of the narrator; as in Matthew 1:21 the bare name is kept where it is used as a name.

decisions.choice: The crowds speak of Jesus with the honorific ("이분", "이시다"); "예언자"
decisions.reason: The crowds that welcomed him honour him; the townspeople's "이 사람" in 21:10 stays plain. "예언자" is the settled Korean Matthew word.

source.text: Καὶ εἰσῆλθεν Ἰησοῦς εἰς τὸ ἱερόν, καὶ ἐξέβαλεν πάντας τοὺς πωλοῦντας καὶ ἀγοράζοντας ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ καὶ τὰς τραπέζας τῶν κολλυβιστῶν κατέστρεψεν καὶ τὰς καθέδρας τῶν πωλούντων τὰς περιστεράς, καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Γέγραπται· Ὁ οἶκός μου οἶκος προσευχῆς κληθήσεται, ὑμεῖς δὲ αὐτὸν ποιεῖτε σπήλαιον λῃστῶν.

records.literal_gloss: And entered Jesus into the temple and cast out all the selling and buying in the temple, and the tables of the money changers he overturned and the seats of the selling the doves, \v 13 and he says to them, It has been written, The house of me a house of prayer will be called, you but it are making a den of robbers.

en.L: And Jesus entered the temple and threw out all those selling and buying in the temple, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} overturned the tables of the money changers and the seats of those selling the doves, \v 13 and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says to them, "It is written, 'My house will be called a house of prayer,' but you are making it a den of robbers."
en.B: Jesus went into the temple courts and drove out everyone who was buying and selling there. He turned over the tables of the money changers and the seats of the dove sellers. \v 13 "It is written," {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} told them, "'My house will be called a house of prayer.' But you are turning it into a hideout for robbers."
en.R: Then Jesus went into the temple area. He forced out all the people who were buying and selling things there. He turned over the tables of the men who exchanged money. He also turned over the seats of the people who sold doves. \v 13 He said to them, "The Scriptures say, 'My house will be called a house of prayer.' But you are making it a place where robbers hide."

es.L: Y entró Jesús en el templo, y expulsó a todos los que vendían y compraban en el templo, y derribó las mesas de los cambistas y los asientos de los que vendían las palomas, \v 13 y les dice: «Está escrito: “Mi casa será llamada casa de oración”, pero {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} la {{plural_you:están haciendo|estáis haciendo}} cueva de bandidos».
es.B: Jesús entró en los atrios del templo y echó a todos los que compraban y vendían allí. Volcó las mesas de los que cambiaban dinero y los asientos de los vendedores de palomas. \v 13 «Está escrito —les dijo—: “Mi casa será llamada casa de oración”. Pero {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} la {{plural_you:están convirtiendo|estáis convirtiendo}} en una guarida de bandidos».
es.R: Luego Jesús entró en el área del templo. Echó fuera a todas las personas que estaban comprando y vendiendo cosas allí. Volcó las mesas de los hombres que cambiaban dinero. También volcó los asientos de los que vendían palomas. \v 13 Les dijo: «Las Escrituras dicen: “Mi casa será llamada casa de oración”. Pero {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} la {{plural_you:están convirtiendo|estáis convirtiendo}} en un lugar donde se esconden los bandidos».

fr.L: Et Jésus entra dans le temple et chassa tous ceux qui vendaient et achetaient dans le temple, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} renversa les tables des changeurs et les sièges de ceux qui vendaient les colombes, \v 13 et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur dit : « Il est écrit : “Ma maison sera appelée maison de prière”, mais vous, vous en faites une caverne de brigands. »
fr.B: Jésus entra dans la cour du temple et chassa tous ceux qui vendaient et achetaient là. Il renversa les tables des changeurs d’argent et les bancs des marchands de colombes. \v 13 « Il est écrit, leur dit-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} : “Ma maison sera appelée maison de prière.” Mais vous, vous en faites un repaire de bandits. »
fr.R: Ensuite, Jésus est entré dans la cour du temple. Il a mis dehors tous les gens qui achetaient et vendaient des choses à cet endroit. Il a renversé les tables des hommes qui changeaient l’argent. Il a aussi renversé les sièges de ceux qui vendaient des colombes. \v 13 Il leur a dit : « Dans les Écritures, Dieu dit : “Ma maison sera appelée une maison de prière.” Mais vous, vous en faites une cachette pour les voleurs. »

sw.L: Kisha Yesu akaingia hekaluni, akawafukuza nje wote waliokuwa wakiuza na kununua humo hekaluni, akazipindua meza za wabadilishaji fedha na viti vya wauzaji wa njiwa, \v 13 {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} anawaambia, "Imeandikwa, 'Nyumba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} itaitwa nyumba ya maombi,' lakini ninyi mnaigeuza kuwa pango la majambazi."
sw.B: Yesu aliingia katika nyua za hekalu, akawafukuza wote waliokuwa wakinunua na kuuza humo. Akazipindua meza za wabadilishaji fedha na viti vya wauzaji wa njiwa. \v 13 Akawaambia, "Imeandikwa, 'Nyumba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} itaitwa nyumba ya maombi.' Lakini ninyi mnaigeuza kuwa maficho ya majambazi."
sw.R: Kisha Yesu aliingia katika eneo la hekalu. Akawafukuza watu wote waliokuwa wakinunua na kuuza vitu humo. Akazipindua meza za watu waliokuwa wakibadilisha fedha. Akapindua pia viti vya watu waliokuwa wakiuza njiwa. \v 13 Akawaambia, "Maandiko yanasema, 'Nyumba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} itaitwa nyumba ya maombi.' Lakini ninyi mnaifanya kuwa mahali pa kujificha majambazi."

vi.L: Và Đức Giê-xu vào đền thờ, đuổi tất cả những người bán và mua trong đền thờ ra, lật đổ bàn của những người đổi tiền và ghế của những người bán bồ câu, \v 13 và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói với họ: "Có lời chép: 'Nhà {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ được gọi là nhà cầu nguyện', nhưng các người đang biến nó thành hang trộm cướp."
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu vào sân đền thờ và đuổi tất cả những người đang mua bán ở đó ra. Ngài lật đổ bàn của những người đổi tiền và ghế của những người bán bồ câu. \v 13 Ngài bảo họ: "Kinh Thánh chép: 'Nhà {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ được gọi là nhà cầu nguyện.' Thế mà các người lại biến nơi này thành sào huyệt của bọn cướp."
vi.R: Rồi Đức Giê-xu vào sân đền thờ. Ngài đuổi tất cả những người đang mua bán ở đó ra ngoài. Ngài lật đổ bàn của những người đổi tiền. Ngài cũng lật đổ ghế của những người bán bồ câu. \v 13 Ngài nói với họ: "Kinh Thánh có nói: 'Nhà {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ được gọi là nhà cầu nguyện.' Nhưng các người đang biến nơi này thành chỗ ẩn náu của bọn trộm cướp!"

ko.L: 그리고 예수께서 성전에 들어가셔서, 성전 안에서 팔고 사는 사람들을 모두 쫓아내시고, 돈 바꾸는 사람들의 탁자들과 비둘기 파는 사람들의 의자들을 뒤엎으셨다. \v 13 그리고 그들에게 말씀하신다. "기록되어 있다. '내 집은 기도하는 집이라 불릴 것이다.' 그런데 너희는 그것을 강도들의 소굴로 만들고 있다."
ko.B: 예수께서 성전 뜰에 들어가셔서, 거기서 사고파는 사람들을 모두 쫓아내셨다. 그리고 돈 바꾸어 주는 사람들의 탁자와 비둘기 파는 사람들의 의자를 둘러엎으셨다. \v 13 예수께서 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "성경에 '내 집은 기도하는 집이라 불릴 것이다' 하고 기록되어 있다. 그런데 너희는 그곳을 강도들의 소굴로 만들고 있다."
ko.R: 그다음에 예수께서 성전 뜰에 들어가셨다. 그리고 거기서 물건을 사고파는 사람들을 모두 내쫓으셨다. 돈을 바꾸어 주던 사람들의 탁자를 엎으셨다. 비둘기를 팔던 사람들의 의자도 엎으셨다. \v 13 예수께서 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "성경에서 하나님께서 이렇게 말씀하셨다. '내 집은 기도하는 집이라고 불릴 것이다.' 그런데 너희는 이곳을 강도들이 숨는 곳으로 만들고 있다!"

decisions.choice: the temple: the courts around the sanctuary
decisions.reason: The word means the whole temple area. The trading took place in the large outer court, open to Gentiles.

decisions.choice: money changers and dove sellers: trades that served the offerings
decisions.reason: Worshipers paid the temple tax in a set coin (17:24), so other money had to be exchanged. Doves were the offering of the poor (Leviticus 5:7; 12:8).

decisions.choice: Isaiah 56:7 and Jeremiah 7:11
decisions.reason: In Isaiah 56:7 God calls the temple a house of prayer for all peoples. In Jeremiah 7:11 God asks whether his house has become a den of robbers, a place where wrongdoers hide and feel safe.

decisions.choice: the temple, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: the temple of God, the reading of many manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts read "the temple of God"; several early ones do not. The meaning is the same. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: My at the start of the quotation, with no span
decisions.reason: God speaks in the quoted words, so "my" would take the deity_pronoun setting; at the start of a sentence it is capitalized either way.

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: hideout for robbers (B); place where robbers hide (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what a den of robbers was: a hiding place for bandits.

decisions.choice: bandidos
decisions.reason: The Greek word is a robber who uses violence, a bandit, not a sneak thief; Jeremiah's picture is of a den where such men hide between raids. "Ladrones" usually means thieves.

decisions.choice: le temple (L); la cour du temple (B, R); chasser (L, B), mettre dehors (R) (for the whole book)
decisions.reason: As the style guide and Mark 11 settle: Jesus acts in the open courts, not in the sanctuary itself (m1), so Balanced and Readable say "la cour du temple"; Literal keeps "le temple". "Chasser" is the everyday word for driving people out; Readable says "mettre dehors", as the English "forced out".

decisions.choice: Dans les Écritures, Dieu dit (R)
decisions.reason: As Mark 11:17: Readable says who speaks in the quoted words, since "Ma maison" is God's house; the English Readable says "The Scriptures say".

decisions.choice: Nyumba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, with a span
alternatives: yangu with no span, as the English
decisions.reason: The English "My" opens the quotation and is capitalised anyway, so it has no span (English decision r-en-1). Swahili puts the possessive after the noun, where it can take the setting.

decisions.choice: majambazi
decisions.reason: The Greek word is a robber who uses violence, a bandit; "jambazi" is exactly that, where "mwizi" is a thief.

decisions.choice: "đền thờ" (L); "sân đền thờ" (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in Mark 11:15 and the style guide: hieron is the temple courts, where the trading was.

decisions.choice: "Nhà {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}" for God's "my house", with the span inside the sentence
decisions.reason: God speaks in the words of Isaiah 56:7; in Vietnamese the pronoun follows the noun and so takes the span, as in Mark 11:17, though the English "My" stands first and has none.

decisions.choice: "성전" (L); "성전 뜰" (B, R), through 21:15; "쫓아내다" (L, B), "내쫓다" (R)
decisions.reason: Hieron is the temple courts around the sanctuary (meaning decision); as in the Korean Mark 11:15, Balanced and Readable say "성전 뜰", and the verb is the one used for casting out demons.

decisions.choice: "내 집" with no span; "강도들의 소굴" (L, B), "강도들이 숨는 곳" (R); present "말씀하신다" (L)
decisions.reason: God's "my" in the quotation needs no span in Korean (no capitals); the den of robbers is worded as in the Korean Mark 11:17. Literal keeps Matthew's present tense of narration.

source.text: Καὶ προσῆλθον αὐτῷ τυφλοὶ καὶ χωλοὶ ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ, καὶ ἐθεράπευσεν αὐτούς.

records.literal_gloss: And came to him blind and lame in the temple, and he healed them.

en.L: And blind and lame [people] came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in the temple, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} healed them.
en.B: Blind and lame people came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in the temple courts, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} healed them.
en.R: People who were blind or could not walk came to Jesus in the temple area, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} healed them.

es.L: Y se {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} acercaron ciegos y cojos en el templo, y los sanó.
es.B: En los atrios del templo se {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} acercaron ciegos y cojos, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} los sanó.
es.R: Personas que eran ciegas o que no podían caminar se acercaron a Jesús en el área del templo, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} las sanó.

fr.L: Et des aveugles et des boiteux s’approchèrent de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} dans le temple, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} les guérit.
fr.B: Des aveugles et des boiteux vinrent à {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} dans la cour du temple, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} les guérit.
fr.R: Des gens qui étaient aveugles ou qui ne pouvaient pas marcher sont venus vers Jésus dans la cour du temple, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} les a guéris.

sw.L: Na vipofu na viwete walimjia hekaluni, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} akawaponya.
sw.B: Vipofu na viwete walimjia katika nyua za hekalu, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} akawaponya.
sw.R: Watu wasioona na wasioweza kutembea walimjia Yesu katika eneo la hekalu, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} akawaponya.

vi.L: Và những người mù và què đến với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} trong đền thờ, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} chữa lành họ.
vi.B: Những người mù và người què đến với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} trong sân đền thờ, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} chữa lành cho họ.
vi.R: Những người mù và những người không đi được đến với Đức Giê-xu trong sân đền thờ, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} chữa lành cho họ.

ko.L: 그리고 눈먼 [사람들과] 다리 저는 사람들이 성전에서 그분께 나아왔다. 그러자 그분이 그들을 고쳐 주셨다.
ko.B: 성전 뜰에서 눈먼 사람들과 다리 저는 사람들이 예수께 나아왔다. 예수께서는 그들을 고쳐 주셨다.
ko.R: 성전 뜰에서 앞을 보지 못하는 사람들과 걷지 못하는 사람들이 예수께 왔다. 예수께서는 그들을 고쳐 주셨다.

decisions.choice: the blind and the lame in the temple: welcomed where they were once kept out
decisions.reason: A saying from David's time kept the blind and lame from the house (2 Samuel 5:8), and the law barred priests with such defects from serving (Leviticus 21:18). Jesus, the Son of David, heals them in the temple.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus.

decisions.choice: "눈먼 [사람들]", "다리 저는 사람들" (L, B); "앞을 보지 못하는", "걷지 못하는" (R)
decisions.reason: The respectful phrases of the Korean Matthew 15:30-31; the older words are now felt as slurs. Literal brackets the noun Korean adds to the first adjective.

source.text: ἰδόντες δὲ οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς τὰ θαυμάσια ἃ ἐποίησεν καὶ τοὺς παῖδας τοὺς κράζοντας ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ καὶ λέγοντας· Ὡσαννὰ τῷ υἱῷ Δαυίδ ἠγανάκτησαν καὶ εἶπαν αὐτῷ· Ἀκούεις τί οὗτοι λέγουσιν;

records.literal_gloss: Having seen then the chief priests and the scribes the wonders that he did and the children the crying out in the temple and saying, Hosanna to the son of David, they were indignant \v 16 and said to him, Hear you what these say?

en.L: But when the chief priests and the scribes saw the wonders that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did, and the children crying out in the temple and saying, "Hosanna to the Son of David," they were indignant, \v 16 and they said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} hear what these are saying?"
en.B: The chief priests and the scribes saw the amazing things {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was doing, and they saw the children shouting in the temple courts, "Hosanna to the Son of David!" They were furious, \v 16 and they said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} hear what these children are saying?"
en.R: The leading priests and the teachers of the law saw the wonderful things Jesus did. They also saw the children shouting in the temple area, "Hosanna to the Son of David!" This made the leaders very angry. \v 16 They said to Jesus, "Do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} hear what these children are saying?"

es.L: Pero al ver los jefes de los sacerdotes y los escribas las maravillas que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} hizo, y a los niños que gritaban en el templo y decían: «¡Hosanna al Hijo de David!», se indignaron, \v 16 y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijeron: «¿Oyes {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} lo que dicen estos?».
es.B: Los jefes de los sacerdotes y los escribas vieron las cosas asombrosas que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} hacía, y vieron a los niños que gritaban en los atrios del templo: «¡Hosanna al Hijo de David!». Se pusieron furiosos \v 16 y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijeron: «¿Oyes lo que dicen estos niños?».
es.R: Los jefes de los sacerdotes y los maestros de la ley vieron las cosas maravillosas que Jesús hacía. También vieron a los niños que gritaban en el área del templo: «¡Hosanna al Hijo de David!». Esto hizo enojar mucho a los líderes. \v 16 Le dijeron a Jesús: «¿Oyes lo que dicen estos niños?».

fr.L: Mais les chefs des prêtres et les scribes, voyant les merveilles qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait faites, et les enfants qui criaient dans le temple et disaient : « Hosanna au Fils de David ! », s’indignèrent \v 16 et {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} dirent : « Entends-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} ce que disent ceux-ci ? »
fr.B: Les chefs des prêtres et les scribes virent les choses étonnantes qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} faisait, et les enfants qui criaient dans la cour du temple : « Hosanna au Fils de David ! » Ils en furent indignés \v 16 et {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} dirent : « Entends-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} ce que disent ces enfants ? »
fr.R: Les chefs des prêtres et les spécialistes de la Loi ont vu les choses merveilleuses que Jésus faisait. Ils ont vu aussi les enfants qui criaient dans la cour du temple : « Hosanna au Fils de David ! » Cela a mis les chefs très en colère. \v 16 Ils ont dit à Jésus : « Entends-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} ce que disent ces enfants ? »

sw.L: Lakini wakuu wa makuhani na waandishi, walipoyaona mambo ya ajabu aliyofanya, na watoto waliokuwa wakilia kwa sauti hekaluni wakisema, "Hosana kwa Mwana wa Daudi," walighadhibika, \v 16 wakamwambia, "Je, {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} unasikia kile ambacho hawa wanasema?"
sw.B: Wakuu wa makuhani na waandishi waliona mambo ya ajabu aliyokuwa akifanya, na waliwaona watoto wakipaza sauti katika nyua za hekalu, "Hosana kwa Mwana wa Daudi!" Wakakasirika sana, \v 16 wakamwambia, "Je, unasikia watoto hawa wanavyosema?"
sw.R: Wakuu wa makuhani na walimu wa sheria waliona mambo ya ajabu aliyofanya Yesu. Pia waliwaona watoto wakipaza sauti katika eneo la hekalu, "Hosana kwa Mwana wa Daudi!" Jambo hilo liliwakasirisha sana viongozi hao. \v 16 Wakamwambia Yesu, "Je, unasikia watoto hawa wanavyosema?"

vi.L: Nhưng khi các thầy tế lễ cả và các thầy thông giáo thấy những việc lạ lùng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã làm, và thấy các trẻ em kêu lên trong đền thờ rằng: "Hô-sa-na Con của Đa-vít!" thì họ bất bình, \v 16 và nói với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Ông có nghe những đứa này nói gì không?"
vi.B: Các thầy tế lễ cả và các thầy thông giáo thấy những việc lạ lùng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đang làm, và thấy các trẻ em reo lên trong sân đền thờ: "Hô-sa-na Con của Đa-vít!" Họ vô cùng tức giận, \v 16 và nói với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Ông có nghe bọn trẻ này nói gì không?"
vi.R: Các thầy tế lễ cả và các thầy dạy luật thấy những việc kỳ diệu Đức Giê-xu làm. Họ cũng thấy các trẻ em reo hò trong sân đền thờ: "Hô-sa-na Con vua Đa-vít!" Điều đó làm các nhà lãnh đạo rất tức giận. \v 16 Họ nói với Đức Giê-xu: "Ông có nghe bọn trẻ này đang nói gì không?"

ko.L: 그러나 대제사장들과 율법학자들은 그분이 하신 놀라운 일들과, 성전에서 "다윗의 자손께 호산나!" 하고 소리 지르는 아이들을 보고 분개하여, \v 16 그분께 말했다. "당신은 이들이 무슨 말을 하는지 듣고 있습니까?"
ko.B: 대제사장들과 율법학자들은 예수께서 하신 놀라운 일들을 보았다. 또 아이들이 성전 뜰에서 "다윗의 자손께 호산나!" 하고 외치는 것도 보았다. 그들은 몹시 화가 나서 \v 16 예수께 말했다. "당신은 이 아이들이 하는 말이 들립니까?"
ko.R: 대제사장들과 율법 선생들은 예수께서 하신 놀라운 일들을 보았다. 또 아이들이 성전 뜰에서 "다윗의 자손께 호산나!" 하고 외치는 것도 보았다. 그래서 그 지도자들은 몹시 화가 났다. \v 16 그들이 예수께 말했다. "당신은 이 아이들이 하는 말을 듣고 있습니까?"

decisions.choice: wonders: the healings just done
decisions.reason: The word means remarkable deeds. It refers back to the healing of the blind and lame (21:14).

decisions.choice: children: boys and girls, young enough to be called infants in 21:16
decisions.reason: The word can mean child or servant. Jesus answers with a verse about infants, so children are meant.

decisions.choice: do you hear: a demand that Jesus stop them
decisions.reason: The leaders expect Jesus to reject the title the children give him.

decisions.choice: leading priests; teachers of the law
decisions.reason: Readable uses the plain names used in 2:4.

decisions.choice: los jefes de los sacerdotes; los escribas (L, B), los maestros de la ley (R)
decisions.reason: The terms used throughout Matthew. Readable says what the scribes were, teachers of the Law, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: wakuu wa makuhani; waandishi (L, B), walimu wa sheria (R)
decisions.reason: The terms used throughout Matthew. Readable says what the scribes were, teachers of the Law, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "Ông" for "you" in the chief priests' and scribes' words, with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: As settled for Matthew (12:2, 12:24): opponents speak to Jesus as "ông"; Jesus answers them as "các người".

decisions.choice: "các trẻ em" (L, B, R)
decisions.reason: Boys and girls, young enough to be called infants in 21:16; "trẻ em" is the plain word.

decisions.choice: The chief priests and scribes speak to Jesus in 합쇼체 but call him "당신"
decisions.reason: Their question is a demand that he stop the children (meaning decision); as in the Korean Matthew 15:1-2, hostile leaders speak formally but keep their distance with "당신". "대제사장들" and "율법학자들" (L, B), "율법 선생들" (R) as settled.

decisions.choice: "놀라운 일들"; "아이들"
decisions.reason: The wonders are the healings just done, and the children are boys and girls (meaning decisions); Korean "아이들" covers both.

source.text: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς λέγει αὐτοῖς· Ναί.

records.literal_gloss: The but Jesus says to them, Yes.

fr.B: Jésus leur répondit : « Oui, je l’entends.
fr.R: Jésus a répondu : « Oui, je les entends.

vi.R: Đức Giê-xu trả lời: "Có, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nghe thấy.

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: I do (B); Yes, I hear them (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable answer the question in full.

decisions.choice: historic present at Literal (les dice); past at Balanced and Readable (les respondió)
decisions.reason: Matthew tells parts of this passage in the present (English decision r-en-1, and verse 13). Literal keeps it, as the English Literal does; Balanced and Readable tell it in the past, as Spanish narrative does.

decisions.choice: historic present kept at Literal (anawaambia); past at Balanced and Readable (akawajibu)
decisions.reason: Matthew tells parts of this passage in the present (English decision r-en-1, and verse 13). Literal keeps it, as the English Literal does; Balanced and Readable use the narrative past.

decisions.choice: "nói" with no "đã" (L) for the historic present, also 21:13
decisions.reason: As elsewhere in Matthew.

source.text: οὐδέποτε ἀνέγνωτε ὅτι Ἐκ στόματος νηπίων καὶ θηλαζόντων κατηρτίσω αἶνον;

records.literal_gloss: Never did you read that Out of mouth of infants and nursing you prepared for yourself praise?

en.L: Have you never read, 'Out of [the] mouth of infants and nursing [babies] {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have prepared praise for {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}}'?"
en.B: Did you never read this: 'Out of the mouths of little children and nursing babies {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have brought forth praise for {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}}'?"
en.R: Surely you have read this in the Scriptures: 'You have made little children and babies sing {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} praise.'"

es.L: ¿Jamás {{plural_you:leyeron|leísteis}}: “De boca de criaturas y de bebés de pecho {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} preparaste alabanza”?».
es.B: ¿Nunca {{plural_you:han leído|habéis leído}} esto: “De la boca de los niños pequeños y de los bebés de pecho has hecho brotar alabanza para {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}”?».
es.R: Sin duda {{plural_you:han leído|habéis leído}} esto en las Escrituras: “Has hecho que los niños pequeños y los bebés canten {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} alabanzas”».

fr.L: N’avez-vous jamais lu : “De la bouche des tout-petits et des [enfants] qui tètent, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}es préparé une louange” ? »
fr.B: N’avez-vous jamais lu ces paroles : “Par la bouche des tout-petits et des nourrissons, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as fait monter pour {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} une louange” ? »
fr.R: Vous avez sûrement lu ces paroles dans les Écritures : “Même les petits enfants et les bébés, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} leur as appris à chanter {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} louange.” »

sw.L: Je, hamjawahi kusoma kwamba, 'Kutoka kinywani mwa watoto wachanga na wanaonyonya umejitayarishia sifa'?"
sw.B: Hamjawahi kusoma maneno haya: 'Katika vinywa vya watoto wadogo na watoto wachanga wanaonyonya umeleta sifa kwa ajili {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}}'?"
sw.R: Hakika mmesoma maneno haya katika Maandiko: 'Umewafanya watoto wadogo na watoto wachanga waimbe sifa {{deity_pronoun:zako|Zako}}.'"

vi.L: Các người chưa từng đọc sao: 'Từ miệng trẻ thơ và [trẻ] còn bú, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã chuẩn bị lời ca ngợi cho mình'?"
vi.B: Các người chưa bao giờ đọc lời này sao: 'Từ miệng trẻ nhỏ và trẻ còn bú, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã khiến lời ca ngợi dâng lên cho {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}'?"
vi.R: Chắc chắn các người đã đọc lời này trong Kinh Thánh: 'Chúa đã khiến trẻ nhỏ và em bé ca ngợi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.'"

ko.L: 너희는 한 번도 읽지 못하였느냐? '어린아이들과 젖먹이들의 입에서 주께서 찬양을 준비하셨습니다.'"
ko.B: 너희는 이 말씀을 읽어 보지 못하였느냐? '주께서 어린아이들과 젖먹이들의 입에서 찬양이 나오게 하셨습니다.'"
ko.R: 너희는 성경에서 이 말씀을 분명히 읽었을 것이다. '주께서는 어린아이들과 아기들이 주님을 찬양하게 하셨습니다.'"

decisions.choice: Psalm 8:2 (8:3 in the Hebrew numbering), in the Greek Old Testament
decisions.reason: Jesus quotes the Greek version, which has "praise" where the Hebrew has "strength". In the psalm God is addressed; Jesus applies the words to the children praising him.

decisions.choice: have you never read: a question that expects yes
decisions.reason: The scribes knew the psalm. Jesus asks whether they have seen what it means, as in 12:3 and 19:4.

decisions.choice: prepared: brought about, made complete
decisions.reason: The verb means to put in order or make ready; with the middle voice, for oneself.

decisions.choice: spans on you and yourself for God
decisions.reason: The psalm speaks to God, so the pronouns take the deity_pronoun setting.

decisions.choice: a statement instead of a question
decisions.reason: The question expects yes; Readable states it, as at other such questions.

decisions.choice: "{{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}" for God addressed in Psalm 8; "Chúa" (R) at the start of the line
decisions.reason: The psalmist speaks to God as "Ngài", as the style guide sets for the Psalms; Readable opens with "Chúa" so that the sentence does not begin with a pronoun.

decisions.choice: Psalm 8:2 addressed to God in 합쇼체 with "주께서", no divine_name span
decisions.reason: The psalm speaks to God (style guide, section 7a: the psalmist speaks to God in 합쇼체); the Greek has no divine name here, so "주" stands without the span, as for Old Testament quotations in the Korean Gospels. Korean has no capitals for the English spans to change.

decisions.choice: "너희는 한 번도 읽지 못하였느냐?" first (L)
decisions.reason: Korean puts the main verb last; Literal asks first and lets the quotation follow, keeping the Greek order of units.

source.text: καὶ καταλιπὼν αὐτοὺς ἐξῆλθεν ἔξω τῆς πόλεως εἰς Βηθανίαν, καὶ ηὐλίσθη ἐκεῖ.

records.literal_gloss: And having left them he went out outside the city to Bethany, and he lodged there.

en.L: And leaving them, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went out of the city to Bethany, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} spent the night there.
en.B: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} left them and went out of the city to Bethany, where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} spent the night.
en.R: Then Jesus left them. He went out of the city to the village of Bethany and stayed there for the night.

es.L: Y habiéndolos dejado, se fue fuera de la ciudad, a Betania, y allí pasó la noche.
es.B: Después los dejó y salió de la ciudad hacia Betania, donde pasó la noche.
es.R: Luego Jesús los dejó. Salió de la ciudad y fue al pueblo de Betania, y allí se quedó a pasar la noche.

fr.L: Et, les laissant, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} sortit hors de la ville vers Béthanie, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} y passa la nuit.
fr.B: Puis {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} les quitta et sortit de la ville pour aller à Béthanie, où {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} passa la nuit.
fr.R: Ensuite, Jésus les a laissés. Il est sorti de la ville et il est allé au village de Béthanie. Il y a passé la nuit.

sw.L: Na akiisha kuwaacha, alitoka nje ya mji akaenda Bethania, na huko akalala usiku.
sw.B: Kisha akawaacha, akatoka nje ya mji kwenda Bethania, ambako alilala usiku.
sw.R: Kisha Yesu aliwaacha. Akatoka nje ya mji, akaenda kijiji cha Bethania, akalala huko usiku ule.

vi.L: Rồi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} rời họ, đi ra khỏi thành đến Bê-tha-ni và nghỉ đêm tại đó.
vi.B: Rồi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} rời họ, ra khỏi thành, đến Bê-tha-ni và nghỉ đêm ở đó.
vi.R: Rồi Đức Giê-xu rời họ. Ngài ra khỏi thành, đi đến làng Bê-tha-ni và ở lại đó qua đêm.

ko.L: 그리고 그들을 떠나 성 밖으로 베다니로 나가셔서, 거기에서 밤을 지내셨다.
ko.B: 그리고 예수께서는 그들을 떠나 성 밖 베다니로 가셔서 거기에서 밤을 지내셨다.
ko.R: 그런 다음에 예수께서 그들을 떠나셨다. 예수께서는 도시 밖으로 나가 베다니 마을로 가셨다. 그리고 거기에서 밤을 보내셨다.

decisions.choice: Bethany: a village on the far side of the Mount of Olives
decisions.reason: Bethany lay about two miles from Jerusalem (John 11:18). Pilgrims at the feasts often lodged outside the crowded city.

decisions.choice: Jesus; the village of
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus and says what Bethany was.

decisions.choice: "베다니"
decisions.reason: The Protestant form of the name (style guide, section 5); Readable says it was a village, as the English does.
